newsitem.title: HUNGARY: EIB sets 120mln ecu loan for Hungary railways.
newsitem.headline: EIB sets 120mln ecu loan for Hungary railways.

text.p: The European Investment Bank (EIB) said on Tuesday its board had approved a 120 million ecu loan to upgrade the efficiency, service and competitiveness of Hungarian railways.
A main goal of the programme will be to improve transit links between Hungary and Western Europe, Romania and the Ukraine, the EIB said.
EIB vice president Wolfgang Roth said that EIB would also expect contributions to the programme from Phare, the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development and Hungary.
"Those are parts of the trans-European network which was decided some two years ago," Roth said at a news conference in Budapest.
"Improving the (rail) infrastructure is a main political priority of the European Union.

The EIB board of directors meeting in Budapest was its first in eastern or central Europe. During the meeting the board, which is the EU's financing institution, approved loans totalling some 2.6 billion ecu, an EIB statement said.
